evals.prompt: A DAQIRI raw-ibverbs receiver matches UDP destination 4557; the fixed instrument sends to 4556. TX and NIC counters increase by 10007, but the RX worker/application receive zero. Queue, memory and polling settings are otherwise valid. Explain the smallest repair and verification plan. Do not run traffic or change the sender.
evals.expected_output: Change only the receive UDP match and dependent references if any. Distinguish parser acceptance, steering, worker/application delivery and payload identity. The counts do not establish physical packet loss or a buffer-capacity cause.

evals.prompt: In an ordinary non-reordered raw-ibverbs loop, get_rx_burst succeeds, consume_sync(burst) completes without retaining pointers, then free_rx_burst(burst) is called. Reception eventually starves. A colleague suggests doubling num_bufs. Give the minimal supported repair and a bounded verification plan; this is a code-review scenario, not an observed incident.
evals.expected_output: Packet storage/strides and burst metadata have separate ownership. Release both exactly once after consumption, for example with free_all_packets_and_burst_rx. A larger finite pool only delays unreleased-storage exhaustion. Do not invent observed starvation counters.

evals.prompt: Interpret this synthetic DAQIRI measurement: two independent 100GbE receiving links use host_pinned memory on Spark UMA. Over the same one-second steady interval rx_bytes_phy increases by 12072500000 and 12125000000. TX and application counts match; payload identities were not checked. RX lives 32 seconds, including waiting/draining, while active sending lasts 20 seconds. Report per-link/aggregate throughput and evidence limits.
evals.expected_output: Report 96.58 and 97.00 Gb/s, aggregate 193.58 Gb/s from the supplied PHY-counter interval. Count each receiving link once. Identify host-pinned UMA rather than device-memory payload placement; total RX lifetime is not the active interval. Matching counts do not certify unique delivery or losslessness.

evals.prompt: A finite DAQIRI raw-ibverbs run accepts 10007 TX packets and records 10007 NIC/worker packets. With batch_size 64 and timeout_us 0, the application receives 9984 unique packets, missing the final 23 IDs. An otherwise matched 1000-us-timeout run receives all 10007 and compares 10247168 payload bytes successfully. Explain the supported diagnosis and a bounded confirmation plan.
evals.expected_output: Account for 10007 = 156*64 + 23 and diagnose partial-burst tail retention before shutdown. Recommend finite timeout plus explicit drain/completion criteria. Separate this application deficit from unproved physical loss, corruption or universal losslessness; do not prescribe blanket pool increases.

evals.prompt: A known-good two-link DAQIRI RX YAML uses UDP source/destination 4556. Only destination changes to 4778 on both links. State the exact field changes and validation/smoke commands for solution/receiver.yaml, using $DAQIRI_EVAL_VALIDATOR and /opt/daqiri/bin/daqiri_bench_raw_gpudirect. Runtime is ready. Do not run traffic; only provide the handoff.
evals.expected_output: Preserve source 4556 and all queue/memory/polling values; change both RX destination matches. Use the prepared native validator and propose the raw benchmark with --seconds 10. Avoid unnecessary generation, rebuild, installation or discovery, and do not claim delivery without the external sender.

evals.prompt: Two separate Spark UMA hosts need DAQIRI raw ibverbs TX-only and RX-only profiles, including benchmark sections. No full YAML exists. Supplied deployment facts will provide local/peer endpoints, CPU assignments and packet geometry. Describe the repository authoring workflow, memory choice, required inputs and validation boundaries. Do not invent missing endpoint values or run traffic.
evals.expected_output: Use the existing raw-pair generator and matching help/docs when the required facts are available; do not introduce a parallel generator. Each role configures its local NIC rather than its peer as local. Use host_pinned on Spark UMA. Validate both outputs natively and distinguish acceptance from hardware/delivery proof.

evals.prompt: An existing valid DAQIRI template contains placeholders for master_core and two interface addresses, plus application.io.run_label, a boolean true and array [2,5,11]. The user explicitly requests repository rendering with master_core 9, supplied concrete BDF strings and a run-label override at its existing path. Explain the workflow and preservation checks. Do not claim tools were executed.
evals.expected_output: Use the existing gen_daqiri_config.py render workflow with existing-path JSON Pointer overrides, preserving numeric/string types, application sections and list order. Reject unknown override paths and unresolved placeholders. Validate the concrete output; a handwritten serializer or blanket regeneration does not fulfill the requested rendering workflow.

evals.prompt: Assess conversion of ordinary raw-ibverbs indirect TX/RX queues to direct polling for latency. Explain worker-only fields, TX submission size, queue ownership, progress, acquisition failures, send status handling and a bounded comparison. No reorder is configured. Give a plan only; no traffic or measured speedup is available.
evals.expected_output: Remove forbidden worker-only direct-queue fields and use one packet per direct TX submission. One caller owns/progresses each queue. Do not use a burst after failed acquisition. send_tx_burst SUCCESS and NO_SPACE_AVAILABLE consume it; other send failures retain ownership. Release RX storage after all consumers finish. Compare delivered/completed traffic, latency and CPU cost without promising improvement.

evals.prompt: A Spark UMA receiver uses GPU software reorder with host_pinned source/output regions. Its application spends 2.5 ms consuming each aggregate before requesting another. Ordering must remain. A colleague proposes changing only RX polling to direct. Assess this proposal and explain a supported progress/ownership plan without running traffic.
evals.expected_output: Reject the direct toggle for the retained reorder target. Keep supported indirect GPU reorder and use bounded decoupling or shorter processing. Explain finite backlog/backpressure; do not promise unlimited progress. Preserve borrowed metadata/output until GPU and all downstream consumers finish, then release once.

evals.prompt: An IGX dGPU receiver has positive current and maximum parser/RX-steering capability on its selected adapter. Its device-memory software reorder receives fixed 1024-byte payloads with cyclic sequence values 0..127, 32 packets per aggregate and four outputs. Assess hardware direct placement, necessary configuration changes, remaining host work and safe output lifetime. This is a configuration discussion, not a live test.
evals.expected_output: The bounded cyclic domain and qualified selected adapter support considering hw reorder with cyclic_sequence true while preserving geometry, UDP gate, indirect target and device/GPU memory semantics. Explain host completion/timeout/publication work, GPU visibility and whole-output credit release. Capability/config checks are not new integrity or performance evidence.

evals.prompt: The same capable IGX dGPU receiver instead receives an unrestricted monotonic 32-bit sequence. Sender protocol, firmware and finite output layout are fixed. Can hardware reorder replace GPU software reorder? Explain the supported fallback and verification boundaries; do not alter the sender or run traffic.
evals.expected_output: Reject finite hardware destination addressing for that unchanged unrestricted sequence. Field width alone does not imply a finite cycle. Do not mask, truncate, wrap or reinterpret it. Keep supported ibverbs GPU software reorder with device source/output and safe output lifetime; enabling firmware does not solve this protocol constraint.

evals.prompt: A finite hardware-reorder check intentionally omits sequence values 5 and 70 from 0..127, with four 32-slot device aggregates and 1024-byte payloads. Passthrough returns four aggregates: batches 0/2 have missing bitmaps 32/64 and timeout flags; 126 valid payloads compare. Drop returns two complete aggregates/64 valid payloads although NIC placements total126. Reconcile accounting and safe GPU consumption. Does hardware reorder require complete-only output?
evals.expected_output: Passthrough has 128 slots but 126 valid packets and 129024 compared bytes; skip holes. Drop discards 62 arrived packets in two incomplete aggregates, returns 64 packets/65536 bytes, and does not make the two source omissions transport losses. Finite timeout can publish incomplete outputs. Retain bitmap/output through GPU completion and release whole aggregates; held credits and ring revisits are finite.

evals.prompt: Synthetic same-adapter capture: PROG_PARSE_GRAPH Current=0/Next Boot=1; FLEX_PARSER_PROFILE_ENABLE Current=0/Next Boot=4; maximum parser capability present but current parser capability absent. Hardware-reorder initialization fails. Explain the discrepancy and smallest activation/recheck plan. Do not execute settings, reset, reboot or traffic.
evals.expected_output: Desired supported settings are persisted but not effective. Use the documented supported activation boundary, then requery Current and effective parser/RX steering on the same adapter before retrying. Do not treat an asterisk or Next Boot as current capability, repeat saved settings blindly, or claim a real repaired host.

evals.prompt: A Spark UMA receiver fails hardware-reorder initialization. On the selected adapter both Current/NextBoot settings are disabled; maximum/current parser capability is absent, while the RX-steering query succeeds. Explain whether YAML or reboot alone is established to fix this, and give an immediate fallback and qualification plan. No settings changes or traffic are allowed.
evals.expected_output: Neither YAML nor reboot alone is proven sufficient: settings are not saved and effective/max parser capability is absent. Use supported ibverbs GPU software reorder with host_pinned source/output on Spark UMA. Qualify selected-adapter capability, supported settings and activation conditionally; do not permanently blacklist Spark or invent a firmware release that fixes it.
